_comment: Authoritative model<->CLI binding. Role-file frontmatter `model:` is intentionally ignored. Command templates use {prompt} and {system} placeholders; tune them once the real CLIs are installed. None of these are assumed present - the orchestrator detects missing commands and fails gracefully. NOTE: the per-agent `roles` list is ADVISORY documentation only (nothing enforces it); which agent fills which role is governed at run time by each workflow's `roster` block in workflows.json (the availability-resolved shift-left chain). `disabled: true` removes an agent from all rosters (the chain shifts left around it).

claude._model_comment: The model MUST be pinned explicitly. Without --model the headless `claude -p` inherits the LAUNCHING session's default model, and on 2026-08-04 that was Fable — which this account cannot use, so every Developer step died in ~1-5s with the misleading 'API Error: Rate limit reached' (zero tokens billed, num_turns 1) while plan usage sat at 43% session / 5% weekly. Four dev runs were lost to it. claude_sonnet/claude_haiku survived the same incident precisely because they DID pin a model. Verified live: `claude -p --model claude-opus-5` -> PONG, unpinned -> rate-limit error.
claude._read_only_comment: read_only_args is used whenever this agent runs a NON-editing role (Code Reviewer, Developer Verifier). bypassPermissions alone still PERMITS edits (it only skips prompts) — a 2026-06-15 inv run aborted when a read-only Claude refuter edited the tree. --disallowedTools hard-removes the edit tools so a read-only role physically cannot author/modify code; Bash/Read/Grep stay available for ssh+log diagnostics, and the git guard remains the backstop against bash-level writes.
claude._timeout_comment: Raised 7200 -> 10800 on 2026-09-13 for CT-1B2-h, the activation atom: its witness ALONE is about an hour now - a dual build (~12 min), the service-equivalence gate (13 min measured, D75.6) and eighteen further gates - and the developer runs its own witness, so a two-hour bound left under an hour for the implementation. Earlier, raised 3600 -> 7200 on 2026-09-12: the CT-1B2-f developer step (the deferred container + checked insertion + fatal-boundary atom) ran the full 3600 s and was killed mid-write, leaving ~2800 lines across 7 files in the tree and returning nothing. The bound is an upper limit, not a target - lighter steps are unaffected - and it is the per-step wall-clock that binds on the heaviest atoms, not the thinking budget, which stays where it is.
claude._env_comment: MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=15000 ('think hard' level) for the Developer. Chosen over 31999 ('ultrathink') because ultrathink made dev steps slow enough to hit the per-step timeout on heavier tasks and is more exposed to session/context rollover; 15000 keeps strong reasoning while steps stay fast. claude CLI has no effort flag, so it is set via env.

claude_sonnet._comment: Claude Sonnet 4.6 as a Claude OPPONENT (Hypothesis Refuter / Adversarial Verifier) — a distinct, lighter Claude model attacking the Opus investigator's hypothesis (intra-family diversity). Runs at MAXIMUM reasoning effort (MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=31999, ultrathink): per Irina 2026-06-15, a Claude assigned to an opponent role always gets max effort so a lighter/same-family skeptic still attacks hard. Read-only; never builds, so ultrathink does not risk a build-step timeout.

claude_reviewer._comment: Opus as the REVIEWER (dev Code Reviewer + arch Developer Verifier) at MAXIMUM reasoning effort (MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=31999, 'ultrathink'). Per Irina 2026-06-15: developers peer-review each other (reviewer=Claude), and since the dev reviewer is the same model family as the developer, we offset the shared-blind-spot risk by running the reviewer at max thinking budget. Read-only; the reviewer never builds (no cargo), so ultrathink does not risk the dev-step timeout that capped the Developer at 16k. Model pinned explicitly — see the claude agent's _model_comment (2026-08-04 unpinned-model incident).

claude_haiku._comment: Claude Haiku 4.5 — the always-available TAIL of every roster chain. Reached only when the stronger members (opus/codex/gemini/deepseek/sonnet) are all unavailable; a lightweight Claude that keeps a workflow running (degraded) rather than aborting. Runs at MAXIMUM reasoning effort (MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=31999, ultrathink) — per Irina 2026-06-15, a Claude in an opponent role always gets max effort; harmless (and helpful) for the judge roles it also covers. Read-only by default; the roster never assigns it the editing Developer/Investigator cell unless it is the only live Claude left.

claude_author._comment: Opus as the implreview AUTHOR (Implementation Architect) at MAXIMUM reasoning effort (MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=31999, 'max effort' per Irina 2026-07-14). Read-only: it OWNS and revises the reviewed artifact but returns the revised TEXT (the engine saves it; parse=False), never editing repo files. A DISTINCT opus agent from claude_reviewer/claude_devops so all three implreview Claude cells (author + 2 peer reviewers) can run at once — one agent cannot fill two roster cells. Model pinned explicitly — see the claude agent's _model_comment (2026-08-04 unpinned-model incident).

claude_devops._comment: Opus as the implreview DEVOPS reviewer (DevOps Reviewer) at MAXIMUM reasoning effort (MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=31999, 'extra high effort' per Irina 2026-07-14). Read-only. A DISTINCT opus agent so the implreview author / developer-reviewer / devops-reviewer cells can all be Opus simultaneously. Model pinned explicitly — see the claude agent's _model_comment (2026-08-04 unpinned-model incident).

codex._read_only_comment: read-only roles (Architect/Code Reviewer/Verifier/Refuter) must NOT write the tree. --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox DISABLES the sandbox so codex CAN edit, relying only on the git-guard — a 2026-06-22 arch-author run aborted HUMAN_REQUIRED when codex wrote the tree. --sandbox read-only physically blocks writes while keeping reads/analysis; codex exec stays headless. --skip-git-repo-check is REQUIRED because the agent cwd is the multi-repo workspace root which is NOT itself a git repo (codex refuses to run in an untrusted/non-git dir otherwise; the old bypass flag implied this skip). Codex equivalent of the Claude --disallowedTools approach above.

gemini._agy_2026_10_10: 2026-10-10 (Irina: 'у гемини теперь подписка'): the subscription is served only through the Antigravity CLI (agy) - the Gemini CLI answers IneligibleTierError for personal Code Assist since 2026-06-18, and the API key stays free tier. agy 1.3.3 in ~/.local/bin, signed in once interactively (token in the OS keyring). Prompt: one NDJSON user event on stdin (--input-format stream-json) - tested with a 300 KB prompt, the last line was read. Output: stream-json; the final `result` event carries status/response/usage, and agy exits 0 on a failed turn, so status != SUCCESS is the error (usage_format agy_stream_json). READ-ONLY: agy has no per-invocation permission flag, so the cell runs under a private HOME (~/.cache/orchestration/agy-home) whose settings.json is copied from config/agy-readonly.settings.json before every run: allow command(*), deny write_file(*) - probed: the file write is refused, a shell command runs; the sign-in survives because it lives in the keyring. --mode plan does NOT stop writes (probed). QUOTA: the subscription has ONE individual quota pooled across every model; it was exhausted on 2026-10-10 by over-large probe prompts (~0.5M input tokens on gemini-3.1-pro-high) and resets about 2026-10-17. Until then the cell answers 'Individual quota reached' (classified quota, roster shifts left). MODEL: gemini-3.8-flash-high; once the quota is back, gemini-3.1-pro-high is the stronger choice for Technical Lead - test with SMALL prompts. The Gemini-CLI/API-key setup (gemini-readonly.policy.toml) is retired.

Operational toggle (environment state, not project configuration).

deepseek._comment: Independent 4th-family ARBITER. Two transports supported: 'api' (key in api_env) or 'cli' (e.g. an Ollama-style local model). (configured here as DeepSeek; a Mistral/Ollama-style transport works the same way.) Model PINNED to deepseek-v4-pro: DeepSeek moved to the V4 lineup (only deepseek-v4-flash / deepseek-v4-pro exist via /models). The legacy deepseek-reasoner/deepseek-chat IDs are now flash-only backward-compat ALIASES (reasoner=v4-flash thinking-mode, NEVER pro) and return 404/400 after 2026-07-24 15:59 UTC. v4-pro chosen for the judge role (complex reasoning / code review). Verified 2026-06-17.
deepseek._comment_2026_08_30: 2026-08-30 (P1): deepseek gains the READ-ONLY 'Developer Verifier' role so it can be the architecture developer_verifier pin's cross-family fallback when the whole Anthropic account is blocked (workflows.json architecture.roster.pinned.developer_verifier). can_edit stays false — the fallback reviews, it never writes — and it is used ONLY on classified account/provider evidence, never because a Claude is merely missing locally. It cannot hold the arbiter cell at the same time (one agent, one cell), so an account-blocked architecture run that reaches arbitration pauses instead of borrowing the judge; that is the trade the pin's `lost_assurance` records.

_comment_2026_08_31: 2026-08-31 (DEV-07, architecture author/reviewer split): the new READ-ONLY role 'Architecture Author' was added to the allowlist of exactly the three agents that already carried 'System Architect' (codex, claude_author, claude_haiku), because those three ARE the eligibility set for the architecture author cell and the split must not change who can fill it. 'System Architect' is deliberately kept on all three: it is still the role of development.architect, which reviews a real diff. The older notes below that describe the arch author cell as role 'System Architect' (see codex _reenabled_2026_08_20 and workflows.json architecture.roster._author_fallback_2026_08_27) are kept verbatim as the historical record; as of this date that cell's role is 'Architecture Author'.
_comment_2026_08_30: 2026-08-30 (P1, failure-domain metadata): `provider` and `availability_group` are non-secret SCHEDULING labels — they carry no key, no account id and no user data. They tell the roster WHICH AGENTS ONE FAILURE TAKES OUT: an agent name covers an agent-specific failure (a wedged CLI, a missing binary), `availability_group` covers everything sharing credentials / a session limit / a spending cap, and `provider` covers the vendor's whole service (a 503/529). All six claude_* aliases share 'anthropic-default-account' because the established account limits hit them together: in 11 of the 16 runs killed by an exhausted cell the block was account-level, so walking claude_reviewer -> claude -> claude_sonnet could not have recovered them at any depth — each alias just re-hit the same cap. An agent that declares neither field defaults both to its own name (test doubles), which keeps unrelated failures isolated. NOTE on the 2026 top comment above: the per-agent `roles` list is no longer advisory — the roster ENFORCES it (an agent that does not declare a cell's role is skipped for that cell, and an agent with no `roles` list at all holds no cell), and a cell marked `requires_edit` in workflows.json additionally requires can_edit=true. The old comment is kept verbatim as the historical record.
